description: Removes an existing NF status subscription by DELETE on the individual subscription resource; in cross-PLMN cases the serving PLMN NRF forwards the delete to the home PLMN NRF using the subscriptionID rules specified.
normative_statements: The NF Service Consumer shall send a DELETE request to the resource URI representing the individual subscription.
The request body shall be empty.
On success, the NRF shall return 204 No Content.
The response body shall be empty.

If the subscription identified by subscriptionID is not found in the list of active subscriptions in the NRF's database, the NRF shall return 404 Not Found with ProblemDetails providing details of the error.
In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code and shall include a Location header pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance.
In a different PLMN, the DELETE request sent to the NRF in the Serving PLMN shall include the identity of the home NRF (MCC/MNC/NID values) as component values of the subscriptionID.
In a different PLMN, the subscriptionID sent to the NRF in the Home PLMN shall not contain the identity of the PLMN.

If the subscription was created in a different NRF in the HPLMN than the NRF in the HPLMN that receives the subscription delete request, the latter shall forward the request towards the NRF in the HPLMN holding the subscription using the information included in the subscriptionID.
The subscriptionID value in the request forwarded to the NRF in the HPLMN holding the subscription shall contain the same value as originally generated by that NRF.

constraints.statement: The NF Service Consumer shall send a DELETE request to the resource URI representing the individual subscription.
evidence: The NF Service Consumer shall send a DELETE request to the resource URI representing the individual subscription.
constraints.why_interesting: Defines the required HTTP method and target resource for unsubscribe.

constraints.statement: The request body shall be empty.
evidence: The request body shall be empty.
constraints.why_interesting: Testable request-body prohibition for DELETE unsubscribe.

constraints.statement: On success, the NRF shall return 204 No Content.
evidence: On success, "204 No Content" shall be returned.
constraints.why_interesting: Required success status code for the operation.

constraints.statement: The response body shall be empty.
evidence: The response body shall be empty.

constraints.statement: If the subscription identified by subscriptionID is not found in the list of active subscriptions in the NRF's database, the NRF shall return 404 Not Found with ProblemDetails providing details of the error.
evidence: If the subscription identified by subscriptionID is not found in the list of active subscriptions in the NRF's database, the NRF shall return 404 Not Found with ProblemDetails providing details of the error.
constraints.why_interesting: Defines the required error handling for unknown subscriptions.

constraints.statement: In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code and shall include a Location header pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance.
evidence: In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return 3xx status code, which shall contain a Location header with an URI pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance.
constraints.why_interesting: Specifies redirect behavior and required Location header.

constraints.statement: In a different PLMN, the DELETE request sent to the NRF in the Serving PLMN shall include the identity of the home NRF (MCC/MNC/NID values) as component values of the subscriptionID.
evidence: For that, step 1 in clause 5.2.2.7.2 is executed (send a DELETE request to the NRF in the Serving PLMN); this request shall include the identity of the PLMN or SNPN of the home NRF (MCC/MNC/NID values) as component values of the subscriptionID (see clause 5.2.2.5.3).
constraints.why_interesting: Cross-PLMN routing depends on subscriptionID encoding and is directly testable.

constraints.statement: In a different PLMN, the subscriptionID sent to the NRF in the Home PLMN shall not contain the identity of the PLMN.
evidence: In this step, the subscriptionID sent to the NRF in the Home PLMN shall not contain the identity of the PLMN (i.e., it shall be the same subscriptionID value as originally generated by the NRF in the Home PLMN).
constraints.why_interesting: Constrains how the forwarded subscriptionID must be transformed before reaching the home NRF.

constraints.statement: If the subscription was created in a different NRF in the HPLMN than the NRF in the HPLMN that receives the subscription delete request, the latter shall forward the request towards the NRF in the HPLMN holding the subscription using the information included in the subscriptionID.
evidence: If the subscription was created in a different NRF in the HPLMN than the NRF in the HPLMN that receives the subscription delete request, the latter shall forward the request received from the NRF in the serving PLMN towards the NRF in the HPLMN holding the subscription, using the information included in the subscriptionID (see clause 5.2.2.5.3).
constraints.why_interesting: Defines mandatory forwarding behavior when the receiving home NRF does not hold the subscription.

constraints.statement: The subscriptionID value in the request forwarded to the NRF in the HPLMN holding the subscription shall contain the same value as originally generated by that NRF.
evidence: The subscriptionID value in the request forwarded to the NRF in the HPLMN holding the subscription shall contain the same value as originally generated by the latter.
constraints.why_interesting: Ensures the forwarded delete uses the original home-NRF-generated subscription identifier.
